By Advs.
 Shri.Lawrence D Cunha-R

 This Motor Accident Claims Appeal Having Been Finally
 Heard On On 10.10.2024, The Court On The Same Day Delivered

 Judgment
The claimants in O.P.(MV)No.209 of 2016 before the 1st Additional Motor Accidents Claims
Tribunal, Thiruvananthapuram, are the appellants herein.
2. The claimants/appellants are the legal heirs of one
Smt.Nagammal.

On 30.05.2013 at 10.45 a.m,
while she was walking along the road margin of Karamana- Kaladi public road, and when she reached near Tahliyal Margi Free Shop, a TATA Mini Lorry bearing Reg. No. KL01/AM-894 knocked her down and sustained serious fractures and head injuries.
Immediately she was rushed to Chelsa Hospital, Kunjalummoodu and then shifted to General Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram.
Though she was refereed to the Medical College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram on the same day she succumbed to injuries.
On the claim being lodged before the tribunal, the insurance company appeared and contested the case stated that the accident was caused due to the negligence of 2024:KER:76008 the deceased.
On behalf of the claimants, Ext.A1 to A13 were marked.
No oral or Kumar.

documentary evidence was adduced on the side of the Insurance Company.

Based on materials recorded, the tribunal framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the deceased Nagammal died in the accident, which was an outcome of rash and negligent conduct of the 1 st respondent as the driver of the offending Mini Lorry bearing Reg.No.KL-01/AM-894?
2. Whether the petitioners are the dependents of the deceased Nagammal?
3.
Are the petitioners entitled to compensation as prayed for?
If so, what shall be the quantum?
4. Who shall be liable to pay the compensation?

5. Reliefs and costs?
3. On a consideration of the materials and evidence are recorded the tribunal granted the following compensation:-

3 deceased Nagammal.
This finding is questioned before this Court in the present appeal.
5. Heard Sri. A.R Nimod, the learned counsel for the appellants and Sri. Lawrence' D Cunha, the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company.
6. The learned counsel for the appellant relied on the judgment of the Division Bench in Joseph v. Faisal [2015 (1) KLT 334].

The learned counsel for the appellant points out that the Division Bench of this Court followed the judgment of the Supreme Court in Arun kumar Agarwal v. National insurance company [2010 (4) KLT 230 (SC)].

entities.text: Arun kumar Agarwal v. National insurance company [2010 (4) KLT 230 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore according to the 2024:KER:76008 learned counsel, the tribunal's findings in issue No.2 is patently erroneous but against the settled law as laid down by this Court as well as by the Honorable Apex court.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company contented that there is no evidence to show that the claimants were depending upon the services of the deceased Nagammal and hence finding on issue No.2 does not call for any interference by this Court by exercise of its appellate powers.
8. I have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar.

9. In Joseph (Supra), the Division Bench of this Court considered the very same question and held that the term 'services' is required to be given a broader meaning and must be construed by taking into account of loss of personal care and attention given by the deceased to her children.

In Thomas George P.(Dr.) and Another v. O. Santha and others [2016(1) KHC 237], a Division Bench of this Court further held that the mere financial dependency is not the criteria while considering a claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: Thomas George P.(Dr.) and Another v. O. Santha and others [2016(1) KHC 237]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. It is to be noted here that the 2 nd and 3rd appellants are the daughters of the deceased Nagammal.

Going by the principles laid down by this Court in Thomas George P.(Dr.) (supra), the dependency of married children on their maternal home is considered to be a relevant criteria while the tribunal considers the question regarding dependency.
As far as the first claimant is concerned, under no stretch of imagination, it could be construed that he is not depended upon his mother.
It is in this context, the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in Arunkumar Agarwal (Supra) and Division Bench of this Court in Joseph (Supra) assumes significance.

Kumar.V vs Viswanathan Nair K on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189409137/
4 12.

In the light of these settled propositions of law, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the findings submitted by the tribunal on Issue No.2 is pertinently erroneous and thus called for interference.
It is thus declared that the claimants are certainly dependence of deceased Nagammal.
13. Having held so, the next question to be considered by this Court is regarding the quantum of compensation the appellants are entitled under the head loss of dependency.

Going by the principles laid down by the supreme court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited (AIR 2011 SC 2951), the notional income of the deceased Nagammal is liable to fixed as Rs.9000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited (AIR 2011 SC 2951)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the multiplier as 5, the compensation is re

- calculated as,
Rs.4,05,000/- [9000x 12 x 5 x  (1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenditure)].
Thus a total compensation of Rs.4,05000/- is arrived, which is the compensation to which the appellants are 2024:KER:76008 entitled under the head loss of dependency.
In the result, the application is allowed.
The appellants are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.4,05,000/-, which will carry interest at the rate of 8% from the date of petition till realisation with proportionate cost.
The insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The claimant shall furnish the details of the bank account to the insurance company for transfer of the amount Sd/-
